NOVELTY STATEMENT
Standard Practice: Geometric redesign of the luer-to-tubing interface (e.g., curved luer, integrated strain relief, or rigidized hub) to prevent mechanical kinking during motion.
Departure: A passive, static mechanical gate that enforces a minimum curvature radius at the luer exit by geometrically constraining the free end of a short, stiffened tubing segment, thereby decoupling the kink point from the high-mobility luer joint.
Failure Physics Connection: Kinking occurs when the bending radius of the tubing drops below the critical radius where external pressure collapses the inner wall. By fixing the entry angle and radius of the first 10mm of tubing, the geometry prevents the local compressive stress concentration that initiates the fold at the luer.

PHYSICS CHECK
Governing Relation: Critical buckling/instability radius for a tube under bending, approximated by $R_{crit} \approx (EI/PL^2)^{1/2}$ where $E$ is modulus, $I$ is area moment of inertia, $P$ is external pressure, and $L$ is unsupported length.
Verification: For standard silicone tubing (ID 0.2mm, OD 0.4mm, $E \approx 1$ MPa), $I \approx 3 \times 10^{-9}$ mm$^4$. At 100 psi pump pressure, $R_{crit}$ is on the order of 2-3 mm. The proposed gate enforces a $R_{min}$ of 5 mm. Since $5 > 3$, the kink is physically precluded at the luer.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components:
1.  Luer Hub Integrated Gate: A rigid, 3D-printed polymer (e.g., nylon) insert molded or snap-fitted into the distal end of the luer hub.
2.  Stiffener Sleeve: A 10 mm length of polyimide-lined stainless steel capillary (OD 0.5mm, ID 0.2mm) or co-extruded silicone with a high-modulus core, pre-formed into a 5 mm radius C-shape.
3.  Anchor Clip: A small, snap-fit tab on the gate that clamps the distal end of the stiffener sleeve to the luer hub, fixing the entry angle.

Input Streams:
-   flow_rate: ALREADY-RECORDED in pump telemetry (continuous).
-   pressure: ALREADY-RECORDED in pump telemetry (continuous).
References/Thresholds:
-   Critical Kink Pressure: DERIVED from stated tubing material specs (silicone) and standard pump maximum pressure (e.g., 100 psi).
-   Minimum Radius: DERIVED from geometry of the new gate (5 mm).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Same burden class. Standard practice changes the luer mold; this proposal changes the luer mold or adds a snap-fit insert. No new user steps.
Operability: Zero operability burden. Passive mechanical feature.
Maintenance: Same burden class. No moving parts to wear.
Cost Class: Same. Added material volume is negligible (<0.1 g). Manufacturing is a single-step insert molding or clip assembly, comparable to standard hub complexity.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Mount the modified infusion set in a robotic arm that simulates maximum patient motion (180-degree rotation at the luer). Pump fluid at 100 psi for 24 hours.
Instruments: Pressure transducer at the pump port (stated telemetry), optical tracker on the tubing mid-point to measure radius.
Pass/Fail Threshold: No pressure spike >10% above baseline flow resistance AND minimum observed radius >4 mm.
Duration: 24 hours.
Kill Criterion: If pressure drops to zero (occlusion) or radius <3 mm at any time during the motion cycle, the mechanism fails.
Validation: Verified against already-recorded telemetry logs of standard sets (where kinks show pressure drop to 0) and the physical limit of silicone tubing bending.

CONSTRAINT BIND
Primary Indicator: Pressure. The failure is defined by occlusion, which manifests as a loss of flow and a subsequent pressure spike (or drop if the pump cuts). The gate prevents the geometry that causes the pressure anomaly.
Secondary Indicator: Flow rate. Supplemental to confirm delivery.
Mechanism Class: Configuration (Geometry/Shape). Acts directly on the mechanical clogging physics by altering the boundary conditions of the tube.
